artworks.title: Atalanta and Hippomenes
artworks.description: In this Baroque masterpiece, oil on canvas now in the Museo di Capodimonte in Naples, Guido Reni freezes the decisive instant of Ovid's foot-race (Metamorphoses 10.560–707). Atalanta stoops mid-stride to snatch one of Aphrodite's golden apples while Hippomenes presses ahead toward the finish, his body twisting away from her. The two nudes form a sweeping diagonal of opposed motion against a darkened sky, their fluttering drapery and outstretched limbs balanced in an almost choreographic counterpoint that became one of the most celebrated images of the myth. A second autograph version hangs in the Museo del Prado, Madrid.

artworks.title: Hippomenes and Atalanta
artworks.description: The French classicist Nicolas Colombel, working in the manner of Poussin, stages the race as a luminous open-air scene (oil on canvas, Liechtenstein collections, Vienna). Atalanta breaks her stride to gather the gleaming golden apples scattered at her feet — the fruit Venus had given Hippomenes to delay the swift-footed virgin — while the suitor surges past her toward victory. Spectators and a classical landscape frame the contest, lending the decisive moment of Ovid's tale a measured, statuesque grandeur.

artworks.title: The Race between Hippomenes and Atalanta
artworks.description: Noël Hallé's vast canvas (over seven metres wide, today in the Louvre, INV 5270) treats the myth on a monumental, almost theatrical scale. Hippomenes races forward at full speed while Atalanta bends to retrieve a golden apple, the two figures set against a sweeping landscape thronged with onlookers and architecture. Painted in the grand-goût history-painting tradition of the French Academy, the work transforms Ovid's contest of love and cunning into a sprawling neoclassical spectacle.
